# Persona layer

A persona adds a voice on top of the Danish system prompt; it never replaces it.
`apps/api/src/prompt/personas.ts` holds the registry, `selectPersona.ts` picks one
persona per customer message by keyword, and `composePrompt.ts` builds what the model
receives inside the api's single `beforeModelResponse` hook:

1. the base prompt from `systemPrompt.ts`, unchanged, byte for byte;
2. the selected persona's `overlay`;
3. the `Dagens dato: YYYY-MM-DD` line in Copenhagen time, from `makeDateHook`.

Because the base prompt comes first and is never edited, no overlay can remove the AI
disclosure, Danish-only, no-guessing or no-mutation rules. A test composes every
registry persona and fails if one of those rules is missing.

## Registry

OLT's voice, values and persona set are not written down anywhere (`KU-16`, `UU-11`), so
the registry ships one persona whose overlay is a guarded placeholder. A test fails the
day real prose replaces `PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER`; update this table in the same change.

[2] "docs/persona.md" section 2:
# Persona layer

## Registry

| Id            | Label          | Text                                                                                                                                                                                              | Written by                      | Danish review                       | `KU-16`                         |
| ------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `olt-support` | `Kundeservice` | `PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER`: "Pladsholder – OLTs tone og værdier er endnu ikke formuleret som skrevet tekst (KU-16/UU-11). Denne tekst erstattes, når klienten har leveret det endelige indhold." | re:cinq, as a placeholder (#26) | Not reviewed; no reviewer named yet | Open: placeholder, no OLT prose |

The overlay is 162 characters. With its two separating newlines it adds 164 characters to
every provider call, up to six per customer turn, and carries no personal data. The
composed prompt with no tool instructions measures 1,562 characters against the 6,000
ceiling.

[3] "docs/persona.md" section 3:
# Persona layer

## Disclosure (EU AI Act Article 50(1))

A persona, named or not, is still an AI system under Article 50(1). It does not exempt
the agent from the disclosure obligation, and attributing an answer to a persona does not
change the disclosure the customer receives. `AI_DISCLOSURE_RULE` comes from
`@support-agent/disclosure` and sits in the base prompt ahead of every overlay; see
[ai-transparency.md](ai-transparency.md). No overlay may claim or imply a human identity,
and a test checks every overlay against a list of such phrases.

## Personal data (GDPR)

Persona choice is never derived from who the customer is. `selectPersona` takes the
registry and the text of the latest customer message, nothing else: no session, no user
id, no customer number. Routing is a case-insensitive keyword match, so the same message
always gets the same persona.

[4] "docs/persona.md" section 4:
# Persona layer

## On the chat surface

The customer sees one thing per answer: the persona's `label`, as the name above an
assistant entry and in its accessible name, `Svar fra Kundeservice`. The id and label
live in `@support-agent/personas`, which both apps depend on and which carries nothing
else. The registry in `apps/api` takes each persona's `id` and `label` from it, so the
face a customer sees comes from the same list that chose the voice.

`overlay` and `match` never leave the server. They are the agent's instructions, so they
stay in `apps/api`; CI builds the web bundle and fails if any overlay, any match keyword
or the name `PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER` appears in it.

The browser matches an assistant entry's `persona` id against `PERSONA_ATTRIBUTION`, a
static map built from the package's labels. An id the map does not know, such as a persona
since removed from the registry, renders the default avatar and no name; the raw id is
never displayed. The only values this path can render are the package's labels, and the
browser neither stores the id nor sends it anywhere.

[5] "docs/persona.md" section 5:
# Persona layer

## On the chat surface

A named persona is still an AI system under Article 50(1). The label is a role,
`Kundeservice`, not a person's name, and the AI disclosure band stays on screen beside it.

## What is stamped

`composePrompt` writes the selected persona's `id` onto `session.activePersona` on every
turn, the fallback persona included. HAL Engine copies it onto each assistant entry as
`persona` when the entry is created, so it is stored with the conversation, sent in the
`entry_upsert` frame. An answer can therefore be traced to the voice that produced it;
the audit rows do not carry the id yet.

The value is always a registry key. It is an id, never the `label` (display text a
reviewer may edit) and never prose, and nothing derived from the customer's text can
reach it: `selectPersona` only chooses among registry entries. Attributing an answer to a
named persona does not touch the Article 50(1) disclosure the customer receives.

Nothing clears the field after the turn; its only reader runs after the write in the same
turn. The write is only correct when `composePrompt` runs inside `beforeModelResponse`.

content.text: {"answer": "Otto picks the persona with `selectPersona(registry, message)`. That function is pure, has no I/O and no classifier call, and is deterministic. It takes only the registry and the text of the latest customer message. It must not take the session, a user id or a customer number, so who the customer is never influences the choice.
